evidence_notes: Letter to a senator claiming the electoral college should be abolished; support is the 2000 Gore/Bush split plus a source-2 Gallup figure (60% prefer direct vote), then a granted-pros paragraph rebutted by faithless electors (1960s Hawaii/Louisiana, Nixon). org 5 (case then concession-rebuttal build on each other, closing adds the Nixon/Carter/Dole consensus rather than restating; sequence not a nameable move so not 6); dev 5 (specific throughout, most support carries an explanation that adds something - 'leaving an unfavored president', 'it can happen again' - but the Gallup figure is left bare); conv 3 (spelling, capitalization and agreement errors accumulate; the 'Granted, that...' sentence needs repair on re-reading); arg 5 (pros acknowledged and answered by showing electors can defect, reaching past the prompt's either/or framing; does not dismantle the strongest pro, so not 6)

Opens pro-electoral-college ('in my favor I would have the Electoral College' because counting is faster) but paragraph 3 reverses to 'I would like to not want the electoral collge to keep going'; support is largely source facts and quotations (538 electors, 25 media markets, Texas Democrats/California Republicans, 2012 turnout). org 2 (position contradicted elsewhere, no functioning frame - begins mid-argument, ends on a turnout statistic that closes nothing, parts follow without recoverable relation); dev 3 (specific figures present but listed not explained, and the last paragraph is unmarked verbatim source phrasing - patchwriting caps at 3); conv 2 (several places where I must guess: '270 s that you can vote for the president', 'each or any electors in your state has his or her own group of electors'); arg 2 (position stated then reversed, so commitment fails at rung 3)

Agrees the author is right that studying Venus is worth the danger; two quoted source passages (silicon carbide electronics lasting 3 weeks; Venus's rocky sediment, valleys, mountains, craters) each followed by a 'See...' inference, plus an undeveloped 'Venus is a star we see at night' unit. org 3 (idea stated early and held, but the star paragraph repeats the intro without adding and trails off mid-job; frame perfunctory); dev 4 (connection stated for the two quoted supports - 'we could look at what happened to it and make sure that doesn't happened to us' - but the third support is neither specific nor explained, and quotes sit alongside rather than inside the writer's sentences); conv 2 (fragments and missing verbs throughout - 'it a star', 'aswhille' - and the opening sentence forces a guess at where one clause ends); arg 4 (one reason genuinely reasoned: study Venus to learn what happened there and prevent it here; dangers noted but never answered)

Agrees citizens should limit car usage; support is Paris diesel/smog data (67% diesel vs 53.3% western Europe, even-odd plates, 22-euro fine) and the Bogota car-free day, both drawn from sources. org 4 (thesis early and held, opening orients and closing closes, but the two body parts - driving ban and car-free day - swap freely); dev 3 (specific figures, but the Bogota sidewalk/rush-hour sentences are unmarked verbatim source phrasing stitched in, and the diesel statistics are listed with no stated bearing - patchwriting caps at 3); conv 3 (fragments, capitalization and agreement errors accumulate; 'the smog cleared enough for the ruling french party' forces a re-read); arg 4 (the 'less fuel used which means less pollution' chain is reasoned; the 'people need the things that pollutes the air' concession is raised but never answered)

Argues the Facial Action Coding System does not belong in schools because it distracts, wastes money, and exposes students to bullying; two source quotations are dropped in without comment and no named case or figure appears anywhere. org 4 (position in the first sentence and held, opening previews and closing restates, both body parts relate, but distraction and bullying swap freely); dev 2 (support general throughout - crowded schools, wasted money, a generic bullied kid - no named case, particular or figure); conv 3 (fused sentences and wrong words - 'too some kids', 'teaching out kids' - accumulate and force re-reading, but meaning is never obscured); arg 4 (the bullying chain reasons why the system harms - revealed emotions to mistreatment to deeper depression - while 'every positive always has a negative' mentions the other side without engaging it)

Argues limiting car use has advantages; support is the Paris even/odd ban lifted early, Bogota's Day Without Cars spreading to Cali and Valledupar, Vauban's parking limits with the Heidrun Walter quote, and the 2013 9% drop plus 57%/70% car-ownership figures, each cited to a source. org 4 (thesis and preview held, closing turns the opening's concession, but the environment and stress paragraphs swap without loss and Vauban recurs across two parts); dev 5 (specific throughout and most support interpreted - the ban's early lifting shows efficacy, Vauban generalized into 'smart planning' - with the 57%/70% figures left to speak for themselves); conv 3 (misspellings accumulate heavily and 'This may because the Internet allow people' and 'many center cities renewal have made' need repair); arg 4 ('emissions are detrimental, so limiting cuts them' is reasoned; the 'a car is considered by many a nessecity' concession is mentioned and returned to but never answered)

Endorses studying Venus on survival grounds - if Earth is destroyed by war we will need somewhere to go, so we must learn what other planets offer - then claims Venus is 'sefest' before conceding we cannot know if it is safe and doubt we would get there in time; no source material is used. org 3 (idea stated by the end of the first unit but the closing undercuts rather than closes, and the second unit contradicts itself within the same part); dev 2 (support general throughout - hypothetical war, same atmosphere, enough room - with no named case, figure or realized example); conv 2 (must guess repeatedly: 'the dangers if presnts', 'Like all the needs to stay alive keep breathing', 'if the un rotates away'); arg 4 (the survival chain states why studying other planets follows, not merely that it does; drift at the end does not block rung 4)

Evaluates the Venus article as well supported, quoting the 'Earth's twin' density/size passage, the ancient-oceans passage and the machine-innovation passage with paragraph citation, and adding a resource-scarcity reason of its own. org 3 (controlling idea stated and held, but two quoted units end mid-thought with no comment and a stray one-line paragraph after the conclusion repeats the resource point without adding); dev 4 (connection stated for the twin quote - Earth-likeness means discoveries and resources - but the other quotes are dropped bare and the framing restates them; quotes sit alongside the writer's sentences); conv 2 (systematic fragments and vocabulary errors that change the sense - 'fine' for find, 'How it was it could have been the most similar planet' - force guessing); arg 4 (one reason reasoned: Earth is running out of resources, so an Earth-like planet is worth researching; the essay otherwise circles its opening)

Argues FACS has no merit in classrooms because the technology is weak; each body part takes one of the source's own supporting claims - Huang on universal expressions, 'most human communications are nonverbal', the Facial Feedback Theory in paragraph 9 - and turns it against classroom use, closing with students gaming the system. org 5 (parts build from outlier failure to epistemic failure to deliberate defeat and cannot swap; the conclusion's 'baseless ethics' ground was never argued, so it falls short of 6); dev 5 (specific and explained throughout - autism and physical-disability cases, the writer's own school norm, the poker-face inference to 'it can't perform its main task' - but the physical-disability case is asserted, not explained); conv 4 (varied, controlled sentences and apt wording, errors visible - enviroment, infront, it's/its - and one clause, 'If it happened to, though', needs repair); arg 6 (governing principle explicit, 'the only true place you can know how somebody really feels is in their mind', applied to a testing case, plus an explicit boundary marking where the position holds)

Calls emotion-reading technology 'the dumbest thing ever', giving three first/second/third reasons that all restate one point - you should not change someone from what they are - and recommending talking to an upset person instead; no source material or example is used. org 3 (opening is a bare thesis with no orientation, the closing collapses mid-sentence, and the second and third reasons repeat the first without adding); dev 2 (support general throughout and partly circular - 'you should not change a photo because thats changing you' - with no case, particular or figure); conv 2 (fused multi-clause run-ons and a closing I must guess at: 'because deep down they know they are, but do you just because someone makes and upset face dosnt always mean they are'); arg 3 (position committed but reasoning asserted, not shown - the look-happy/be-happy distinction is left for the reader to connect, and the essay circles its opening)
